description: Thermal power station: ordered source energy conversions, transmission-line heating branch and the three alternative user conversions. This is an instructional flowchart, not a measured apparatus or exhaustive efficiency balance.

authoritativeText.text:
**电能的利用** 原书把能量的消费水平①看作社会生产力发展的重要标志，并指出电能是常用而方便的能量利用形式，在生产和生活中起着重要作用。
原书作了一个增长速度的比较：如果世界能量消费每 $25$ 年增加一倍，而电能消费平均每十年增加一倍，就意味着越来越多的用能过程转向电能。
这是原书采用的历史比较，不是今天的统计结论或对未来增长速度的保证。

① 所谓能量“消耗”，不是能量本身消失，而是把能量转化为便于利用的形式。
经过使用，能量最终主要转化为内能，也就是原书所说的热能。

原书描述当时的用电结构时指出：工业是其所称“我国”的主要电能用户，约占电能消费的 $70\%$。
运输也是重要用户，越来越多的铁路线采用电力牵引。
原书还记载，几乎所有集体农庄和国营农场都从国家的发电站获得电能，用于生产和生活。

住宅照明和家用电器也是电能的常见用途。
这里保留原书的用电比例和历史机构名称，不把它们当作现代各国共同的用电结构。

原书指出，当时利用的电能有很大一部分转化为机械能，工业中广泛使用电动机带动机械。
电动机能够方便、紧凑地提供机械运动，从而有利于生产自动化。

原书记载，工业消费的电能约有 $1/3$ 用于电焊、电加热、熔化金属和电解等过程。
这些用途说明，电能不仅可以转化为机械能，也可以用于加热和其他生产过程。

**电能的生产** 原书讨论的各类电站，主要利用机电式感应发电机产生电能。
本段比较火电站和水电站：两者都使发电机转子旋转，但带动转子的动力来源和原动机不同。

火电站的能源来自燃料，原书列举煤、可燃气、石油、重油和油母页岩。
原书把发电机转子的驱动设备分为蒸汽轮机、燃气轮机或内燃机。

原书认为大型火电站最为经济，并记载其所称“我国”的大多数火电站以煤粉为燃料。
书中的例子是，生产 $1$ 千瓦小时的电能需要消耗几百克煤；
这不是各种现代电站都适用的固定耗煤量。

在所描述的蒸汽锅炉中，燃料释放的能量有 $90\%$ 以上传给蒸汽。
蒸汽流在汽轮机中把动能传给转子，汽轮机的轴与电机的轴刚性连接。
原书在此将后者称为“电动机的轴”，随后又叙述汽轮发电机；

这里保留这一源书措辞，本段讨论的仍是机械能传给发电设备的过程。
原书给出的汽轮发电机转速约为每分钟几千转。

原书联系九年级的热机知识，说明提高工质的初始温度有利于提高热机效率；
这一比较还受其他工作条件影响。
书中描述进入汽轮机的蒸汽具有很高的参数：温度接近 $600$℃，压强接近 $300$ 大气压。

所举火电站的效率达到 $40\%$，其余能量中有很大一部分随高温废汽排出。
这里的“损失”是未转化为所需电能，不是能量消失。
能量转换关系见图 $61$。

**热电中心**把废汽中相当大的一部分能量用于工业和生活供热，例如暖气和热水供应。
原书把这类电站的效率记为 $60$-$70\%$；
理解这一比较时，应把供出的电能和有用热量一起考虑，不能把这个数值只当作发电效率。

原书还记载，当时其所称“我国”的热电中心所发电能约占全部电能的 $40\%$，并为 $800$ 多个城市供电和供热。
这些比例和城市数量是保留的历史数据，不是当代统计。

原书评价苏联在其所称“暖汽设备”方面处于世界动力技术的领先地位。
这是源书对当时技术状况的历史评价，不是本课对今天各国技术水平作出的排名。

在水力发电站中，堤坝提高水位，使水具有可以利用的重力势能。
水流带动水轮机，水轮机再带动发电机转子旋转。

原书指出，电站功率与堤坝提供的水位差，也就是水头，以及每秒通过轮机的水量，也就是流量，有关。
能量转换关系见图 $62$。

**原子能电站** 原书描述核能发电在其写作时期开始发挥越来越大的作用。
书中记载，世界上第一个原子能发电站于 $1954$ 年在其所称“我国”建成。
这里保留的是原书的历史叙述和年份，“开始”不是对今天发展阶段的判断。

**高频电流的应用** 在原书列举的许多技术用途中，使用振荡频率为几万或几十万赫兹的交流电较为方便。
本节把这样的电流称为高频电流；
这是本节所用的频率范围，不是适用于所有领域的唯一分类界限。

高频电流通过线圈时，会产生快速变化的磁场，并在放入线圈的导体中产生交变的感生电动势和涡电流。
涡电流可以使导体变热，在合适条件下还可以使金属熔化。
原书列举在真空中熔化特别纯的金属作为这种方法的用途。

原书说明，在所讨论的条件下，频率越高，涡电流越集中于导体表面。
利用这种效应，可以迅速加热零件的外表面，而使内部在这段加热过程中仍保持较冷。

随后迅速冷却，可以得到表面层硬度较高而内部仍保持韧性的淬火零件。
原书记载，这类零件广泛应用于机器制造。

电容器的高频电场也可以用于加热电介质，原书以电介质分子的振动说明这种加热过程。
与前面强调导体表层的用途不同，这里讨论向材料内部传递能量，使材料内部也受到加热。

具体的加热深度和均匀程度取决于材料及工作条件，不应把原书“所有深度都被加热”的表述理解为任何材料都完全均匀受热。
原书列举烘干木质和陶瓷制品等用途。

高频电流和高频场也有医学用途，原书描述它们可以使人体某些部分的表面或深处受热。
这里介绍的是医学中利用电能加热的原理，不是自行进行高频治疗的操作指示。

**Use of electrical energy** The source treats the level of energy consumption① as an important indicator of productive capacity and describes electricity as a common, convenient form of energy use.
It compares growth rates: if world energy consumption doubles every $25$ years while electricity consumption doubles on average every ten years, more energy-using processes are shifting to electricity.
This is the source's historical comparison, not a present-day statistic or a guarantee about future growth.

In its account of electricity use at the time, the source identifies industry as the main user in the country it calls “our country,” accounting for about $70\%$ of electricity consumption.
Transportation is another important user, with increasing use of electric traction on railways.

The source also records that almost all collective farms and state farms receive electricity from state power stations for production and everyday use.
Residential lighting and household electrical appliances are further common uses.
The share and institutional names are preserved as historical information, not a description of every modern country's electricity use.

The source states that a large part of the electricity used at the time is converted into mechanical energy, with electric motors widely driving industrial machinery.
Motors can provide motion conveniently and compactly, helping make production automation possible.

The source records that about $1/3$ of industrial electricity consumption is used for welding, electric heating, melting metals, electrolysis, and related processes.
These uses show that electricity serves heating and other production processes as well as mechanical motion.

**Production of electrical energy** The power stations discussed by the source mainly produce electricity using electromechanical generators based on induction.
It compares thermal and hydroelectric stations: both turn a generator rotor, but the energy source and prime mover driving the rotor differ.

The source describes large thermal stations as the most economical and records pulverized coal as the fuel of most thermal stations in the country it calls “our country.”
Its example uses several hundred grams of coal to produce $1$ kilowatt-hour of electricity;

this is not a fixed coal requirement for every modern station.
In the steam boiler described, more than $90\%$ of the fuel's released energy is transferred to the steam.

In the turbine, the steam flow transfers kinetic energy to the rotor, and the turbine shaft is rigidly connected to the shaft of the electrical machine.
The source calls the latter the “motor's shaft” here and then describes a turbogenerator;

this wording is retained as source wording, while the paragraph concerns mechanical energy being delivered to generating equipment.
The source gives a turbogenerator speed of several thousand revolutions per minute.

Referring to the ninth-grade discussion of heat engines, the source explains that a higher initial working-fluid temperature can support greater efficiency;
other operating conditions also matter.

It describes steam entering the turbine at a temperature close to $600$ degrees Celsius and a pressure close to $300$ atmospheres.
The thermal-station example reaches an efficiency of $40\%$, with much of the remaining energy leaving in hot exhaust steam.

Here “loss” means energy not converted into the desired electricity, not energy disappearing.
The energy conversions are shown in Figure $61$.
Figure 61

**Combined heat and power stations** use a substantial part of the energy in exhaust steam for industrial and household heat, including space heating and hot water.
The source gives an efficiency of $60$-$70\%$;

this comparison should include useful heat as well as electricity, rather than treating the figure as electrical efficiency alone.
It also records that these stations provided about $40\%$ of total electricity in the country it calls “our country” and supplied electricity and heat to more than $800$ cities.
The shares and city count are historical data retained from the source, not current statistics.

The source describes the Soviet Union as a world leader in the heating equipment it discusses.
This is the source's historical evaluation of technology at the time, not a ranking of countries today.

At a hydroelectric station, a dam raises the water level, providing gravitational potential energy that can be used.
Flowing water drives a water turbine, which turns the generator rotor.

The source relates station power to the water-level difference, called the head, and to the volume of water passing through the turbine each second, called the flow rate.
The energy conversions are shown in Figure $62$.
Figure 62

**Nuclear power stations** The source describes nuclear generation as beginning to play a growing role when the book was written.
It records the world's first nuclear power station as having been built in $1954$ in the country it calls “our country.”

This preserves the source's historical account and year;
“beginning” is not a description of the current stage of development.

High-frequency current in a coil produces a rapidly changing magnetic field, inducing an alternating electromotive force and eddy currents in a conductor placed inside.
The eddy currents heat the conductor and can melt metal under suitable conditions.
The source gives melting especially pure metals in a vacuum as an application.

For the conditions discussed, the source explains that eddy currents become more concentrated near the conductor's surface as frequency increases.
This can rapidly heat a part's outer surface while its interior remains relatively cool during the heating interval.

Rapid cooling can then harden the surface layer while the inner layers retain toughness.
The source records widespread use of such hardened parts in machine manufacturing.

inventory.description: Left tall rectangular panel, caption below: thermal power station. Five vertically ordered labels: fuel energy; steam internal energy; steam mechanical (kinetic) energy; turbine mechanical (kinetic) energy; electrical energy. Four downward arrows connect successive stages.

A horizontal rightward arrow leaves the generation panel boundary and enters the user panel boundary. Transmission line label sits above it. A branch from approximately the middle of that line points downward into a separate small rectangular panel labelled conductor internal energy.

Right tall rectangular panel, caption below: users. Three numbered, vertically ordered entries: 1 motor mechanical energy; 2 heater internal energy; 3 storage battery internal energy. No interconnecting arrows between these entries.

Modern addition: horizontal source panels are stacked vertically for readable inline mobile display. The transmission arrow exits the completed generation panel, and its conductor branch remains a branch, not a serial stage. Hidden ports and rectangular spacing are layout construction, not source measurements. Water potential energy is gravitational in the bound edition prose. Storage battery internal-energy wording is retained from source, not replaced with a new chemical-energy label. No efficiencies, measured data, apparatus artwork, heat-recovery arrows, or new energy stages are introduced.
